findings.claim: The passage's ninety-day retention rule does not reconcile with the disposal cadence it states, and the paragraph-3 'exception' presupposes a rule the passage has already abandoned.
findings.evidence: P1 S1-S2: 'The lost-property office behind the bus station keeps what it is handed for ninety days. Clothing then goes to a charity shop, phones and cameras to a saleroom, and the umbrellas ... into a bin bag' - the 'then' places disposal at the ninety-day mark. P1 S4: 'the umbrella rack is cleared twice a year and the rest of the room once' - i.e. non-umbrella items are physically disposed of at most once every twelve months and umbrellas once every six, both longer than ninety days. P3: 'Keys are kept past the ninety days, in a tin, because nobody there can quite bring themselves to throw away a stranger's front door' - framed as a deliberate exception, which presupposes that everything else IS gone at ninety days. Under the charitable reading (ninety days = claim window, clearance lags), the P3 sentence loses its force entirely: on a once-a-year clear-out every item in the room is 'kept past the ninety days', so keys are not exceptional. The three statements cannot all hold.
findings.why: Integrated review's remit explicitly covers 'a number that won't reconcile' and self-contradiction across passage parts. No key is affected - gap (1)'s 'Predictably' still rests on the intra-sentence comparison (umbrella rack cleared more often than the rest of the room), which survives the mismatch - so this does not overturn the MINOR_NOTES verdict; it is the kind of note that verdict names, and the terse record carries no findings payload showing it was seen.

findings.claim: reviews/integrated.jsonl records two contradictory verdicts for elf-b17-002 with no field that establishes which supersedes the other.
findings.evidence: Line 3: {"candidate_id":"elf-b17-002","stage":"integrated","verdict":"INCONSISTENT","reviewed_by":"integrated-review/opus","date":"2026-08-26"}. Line 7: identical except "verdict":"MINOR_NOTES". Same stage, same reviewer, same date, no timestamp, run id, or supersedes key. The resolution order is recoverable only from filesystem mtimes (candidates-final/elf-b17-002.json 13:25, integrated.jsonl 13:30), not from the record. language.jsonl and pedagogy.jsonl additionally carry byte-identical duplicate lines for this unit (language lines 1 and 8; pedagogy lines 1 and 9).
findings.why: A downstream consumer reading the stage record for elf-b17-002 gets both INCONSISTENT and MINOR_NOTES with no tiebreak, so the recorded verdict for this unit is not machine-determinable. The same pattern appears on las-b17-002, so it is systematic rather than a one-off transcription slip.
